newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 1.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on August 1. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said there was no need for Indonesia to be suspicious of the proposal by South African President Nelson Mandela to free jailed East Timorese resistance leader Xanana Gusmao.

The government, the military and the ruling Golkar party has sent a high level team to the Irian Jaya capital Jayapura to investigate why Golkar members of the provincial parliament are boycotting the local legislature.
A leading economist Anwar Nasution has warned that Indonesia's banking sector is sick and is a potential "time bomb" which could have significant affects on the economy in the future.
President Suharto has not yet received a letter from South African President Nelson Mandela suggesting that jailed East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao should be freed.

Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo has said bilateral negotiations between Indonesia and the United States over the issue of Jakarta's national car policy have failed and the dispute will be settled by a panel of the World Trade Organisation.
